title: Sub-Gaussian random projections give a Johnson–Lindenstrauss embedding
statement:
Let $k \ge 1$, and let $A$ be a random $k \times d$ real matrix defined on a probability space $(\Omega,\mu)$, so that for each $x \in \bbr^d$ the image $Ax \in \bbr^k$ has coordinates $(Ax)_1,\dots,(Ax)_k$. Suppose that for every $x \in \bbr^d$ these $k$ coordinates are independent, and that each coordinate $(Ax)_i$ is sub-Gaussian with variance proxy $\|x\|^2/k$, in the sense that $t \mapsto e^{t(Ax)_i}$ is integrable and its moment generating function obeys $\E\!\left[e^{t(Ax)_i}\right] \le \exp\!\bigl(\tfrac{\|x\|^2}{k}\cdot\tfrac{t^2}{2}\bigr)$ for all $t \in \bbr$, and moreover has second moment $\E\!\left[(Ax)_i^2\right] = \|x\|^2/k$. Fix $0 < \varepsilon < 1$ and a finite set $V \subseteq \bbr^d$ satisfying the union bound $|V|^2 \cdot 2\exp(-k\varepsilon^2/8) < 1$. Then there exists a linear map $f : \bbr^d \to \bbr^k$ that is an $\varepsilon$-JL embedding of $V$: for all $u,v \in V$,
\[
  (1-\varepsilon)\,\|u-v\|^2 \;\le\; \|f(u)-f(v)\|^2 \;\le\; (1+\varepsilon)\,\|u-v\|^2.
\]
hypotheses_covered: A is a measurable random k×d matrix on a probability space
for each x, the coordinates (Ax)_i are independent
each (Ax)_i is sub-Gaussian: exp(t(Ax)_i) integrable and mgf ≤ exp((‖x‖²/k)·t²/2)
replaced:
Sub-Gaussian analogue of \texttt{johnson\_lindenstrauss\_of\_gaussian}: the Gaussian
entry hypotheses are replaced by the assumptions that each row projection
$(Ax)_i$ is sub-Gaussian with parameter $\|x\|^2/k$ and has variance exactly
$\|x\|^2/k$.  Under the same failure-probability bound
$|V|^2 \cdot 2\exp(-k\varepsilon^2/8) < 1$, an $\varepsilon$-JL embedding of
$V$ is guaranteed to exist; this covers, for instance, Rademacher ($\pm 1/\sqrt{k}$)
matrices.
